utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-98-34-T, the Prosecutor versus Martinovic and Naletilic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good morning, everybody. It's a long time since we last met each other in this courtroom. What we want to say is happy new year to all of you, including all those people in the booth. Mr. Martinovic, can you hear the proceedings in a language you understand? THE ACCUSED MARTINOVIC: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: No?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Doesn't work, Your Honour. We get nothing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Are you okay? Mr. Martinovic, I'm sorry for keeping you waiting for that long because of the technical problems. Did you have a good Christmas? Do you have anything to complain during this period? THE ACCUSED MARTINOVIC: No, Your Honour, nothing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much, you may sit down.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Testing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Naletilic. THE ACCUSED NALETILIC: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Do you hear the proceedings in a language that you understand? THE ACCUSED NALETILIC: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: How about your Christmas? Do you have anything to complain? THE ACCUSED NALETILIC: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may sit down, please. Now, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, we have problems on our side as well.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: The ones that are built into the...

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. President, the consoles that are built into the table do not seem to be working, at least not at this station, but this does. I may find myself getting pulled away, I'm afraid, but we'll manage. Mr. President, Your Honours, good morning and welcome back. The first witness that we have this morning is named Anton Van der Grinten. He is a Dutch army officer who was an ECMM monitor in Mostar in the second half -- well, approximately from the end of May until August of 1993. He is not testifying or seeking any protective measures, therefore, he will testify in open session. His testimony goes primarily to Background Matters, paragraphs 10 and 11; General Allegations, paragraph 21; count 1, paragraph 26 to 28, 34; and count 18, paragraph 54. I might add that a number of documents or exhibits will be used with this witness, and binders, a binder of exhibits have been tendered to everyone, hopefully, in the courtroom and to the booths, is my understanding. So I hope, Mr. President, that you and Your Honours have those available to you. If not, then they should be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much for this information. Would you please furnish the Court and the Defence counsel with the new list of witnesses you're intending to call for this week.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I will provide that today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Usher, would you please call the witness in.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, I might comment that although Mr. Van der Grinten is a native Dutch speaker, as you might appreciate by now, he speaks, as many Dutch do, fluent English and will be testifying in English and that's -- that was discussed with him and he's comfortable testifying in English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Mr. Meek?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, good morning, and from the Defence bar, we would say Happy New Year to you also. Preliminarily, Mr. Scott was nice enough to just now supply Defence counsel with a list of proposed exhibits that he intends to introduce through this witness. I would, for the Court and for the record, request that we be allowed to cross-examine this witness at a time other than today for the reason that this Trial Chamber, last year, entered an order that all exhibits be translated to a language which our clients can understand. Until a few minutes ago, we had no translations in Serbo-Croatian. Our client, Mr. Naletilic, has not had a chance to review any of these documents, therefore, and obviously will not have a chance -- they are -- the documents I see now are translated into the language he understands but because it was at the last moment before trial started this morning, Mr. Naletilic will not be able to review those documents and assist in his Defence until he can review the same, and that won't happen until after court today, at the very latest, because we've just received the same in Serbo-Croatian this morning. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Shall we proceed with this witness first?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: We don't have an objection to proceeding with the witness. Our request is that we be allowed to cross-examine him at another moment, another date, as he is living in the country, we believe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Happy New Year.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Happy New Year to you, too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you please make the solemn declaration, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You may sit down, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, I feel I must comment very briefly two things I will address further when the Chamber requests it and affords me the opportunity, counsel's comments, and specifically I must advise the Chamber this morning that because of other duties this witness is not in fact stationed in the Netherlands, he is stationed in Turkey, he must return on Wednesday and therefore he will not be available after tomorrow afternoon at this time. Examined by Mr. Scott:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, initially, I'm going to take you through some background material and, with the Chamber's permission, I hope, I will lead you through some of this information quite quickly until we get to more central parts, perhaps, of your testimony. Mr. Van der Grinten, or I should say perhaps Colonel, you attended the Netherlands Royal Military Academy from 1971 to 1975; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you have been in the Royal Netherlands Army since that time?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand that your first mission abroad on behalf of the United Nations was with something called UNIFIL, which I'll ask you to comment on briefly in a moment, from 1979 until 1980 in Lebanon. Can you just very briefly tell the Chamber, so they can understand your background, what was UNIFIL?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: UNIFIL was the UN Interim Force in the Lebanon, and it was actually the first mission of the Dutch Royal Army for the UN abroad. We stayed there for eight years, five years with an infantry battalion and another three years with a unit on company level and I was actually in the 2nd Battalion, the single officer in the rank of captain at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And again, you were there from approximately 1979 to 1980?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: I was there, serving for half a year.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Then you were also for a time in the years 1986 and 1987 you were an UNTSO observer in Lebanon, Syria and Israel; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And again, what was the UNTSO?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: The UNTSO, we call it actually, is the UN Truce Supervision Organisation and one of the oldest UN missions who are dealing with all the agreements between Israel and the Arab countries in the Middle East, so it is a mission where military men, officers I have to say, are controlling the borders and crossing points between the confrontation lines, actually.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And is it correct, sir, that at the present time you have the rank of Lieutenant Colonel in the Royal Netherlands Army and your present assignment is in connection with NATO; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: That's correct. I'm serving at the subregional NATO HQ in Turkey, Izmir; Izmir, Turkey.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is your position?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: My position is I'm chief of the OPS branch of that headquarters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And just so the record is clear, when you say "OPS branch," you mean operations?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Yeah, I'm sorry about that but I will limit my abbreviations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Now, Colonel, with that background, let me take you back, please, to approximately May of 1993. At that time, you were a major in the Royal Netherlands Army and you were serving at that time as part of an ECMM monitoring mission in Hungary; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And directing your attention to about the 21st of May, 1993, did you receive instructions or orders that you were to report to an ECMM mission in about Mostar in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you travelled then to the ECMM headquarters in Zagreb. Croatia, on the 22nd of May, 1993, to receive further instructions.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you briefly tell the Chamber, during this process of making the transition from Hungary to arriving, ultimately, in Siroki Brijeg some days later, what sort of orientation and briefing did you receive in connection with the mission on which you were about to embark?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Okay. Initially, I started in southern Hungary in Seget. That was, of course, the periphery of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Late May, I got the order and the transfer to Bosnia due to a lack of personnel, and I think experienced personnel, and that was the reason that they called me back to Zagreb. There I got, from ECMM at the HQ, the instructions and the brief about the situation in Bosnia and especially Mostar, and I was appointed to be the first monitor, Dutch monitor, actually, in Mostar and went, after that weekend, via Split to Siroki Brijeg where at that time the coordination centre Mostar was situated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, your area of responsibility included Mostar; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Sorry?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your area of responsibility included Mostar?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: It was actually the city, downtown Mostar, yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And why were you located or stationed actually in Siroki Brijeg at that time?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Well, at that time, of course, for security reasons, they transferred the CC from Mostar to Siroki Brijeg.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And we are going to talk a little bit about the ECMM structure, for the Chamber's benefit, in a couple of minutes but you arrived then in Siroki Brijeg on approximately the 24th of May 1993; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now you've made reference already to something called the ECMM coordination centre in Mostar, and in ECMM terminology, and the Chamber will see this on documents, I believe today, was Coordination Centre frequently abbreviated as CC?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there already -- were there already ECMM monitoring teams in Herzegovina when you arrived?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Absolutely, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Approximately how many teams were they and where were they primarily located?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: When you are talking about Bosnia-Herzegovina, there was various teams, the exact number I don't recall now, but...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Specifically in the Mostar region.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: In the Mostar region, actually, four and when I started actually three. That means there was M1 in Jablanica, M2 was the Mostar team, and M3 was the team for the area of south of Mostar located in Medjugorje. Three teams, and later on there came another team in Livno, Tomislavgrad. But that was at the end of my tour, actually.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Specifically, team M2 was the Mostar monitoring team; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you served in team M2 during the entire time of your in the Mostar region?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: All the time, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time that you arrived in Siroki Brijeg, can you tell the Chamber, please, who was the superior officer, the person in charge of the Mostar coordination centre?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Well, at that time, it was a German retired colonel, his name was Klaus Nissen, and he was in charge of the CC Mostar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: And let's say responsible for the output of the three teams.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it correct, sir, just looking ahead a bit, that in approximately early July 1993, Colonel Nissen was followed in this position as the head of CC Mostar by a British -- retired British officer named Sir Martin Garrod?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the ECMM organisational structure, above the coordination centres, the CCs, was there something called a regional centre?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: That's correct. The structure was everywhere the same, and in our particular area, RC Zenica was manned by a full ambassador and at that time, Jean-Pierre Thebault, a career ambassador, French from France.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So in your chain of command, so to speak, CC Mostar reported to RC or regional centre Zenica, which is located more in Central Bosnia north of Sarajevo; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Excuse me, could the speakers make a pause between answer and question. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear that?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Because we are both speaking in English, we both tend to go quickly between --

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: We are too fast.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- question and answer.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Colonel, can you explain to the Chamber briefly what ECMM's mission was in the Mostar region at that time.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Well, the main aim of the mission was to monitor the situation all over in Bosnia and especially, in my case, the Mostar area. I have to say that ECMM was, of course, a political organisation with a non-military structure but only in the field, let's say. The field work, was done by most international officers and sometimes a diplomat but only on the RC level you will find actually ambassador's level.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Monitoring the situation, working on all the international agreements at that moment, and of course trying to improve the agreements, let's say, on the overall political level, but especially a lower level in the area of operations, the agreements between all parties involved. That was one important point. And for the rest, to coordinate with IOs, international organisations, and NGOs, non-government organisations, to make clear what was going on in the area, actually, for ECMM, the head of mission in Zagreb who was reporting every 24 hours to all the AU governments.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. You said a moment ago that ECMM was a political organisation. It might assist the Chamber if I put the question to you this way: How was the mission of ECMM different than the mission of UNPROFOR, the UN military force, if you will?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Well, we were dealing on the political level, actually, and had both access to the political authorities and military, depending on the situation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, during the time that you were on duty in the Mostar region, did you work primarily with a Spanish monitor, a major from the Spanish army, named Jesus Armatriain?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: That's correct. Due to the situation that UNPROFOR, who was monitoring the situation for the UN, but with military units, the area of responsibility where Mostar was situated in was the area of the Spanish Battalion. And due to that situation, all the teams who were operating in that area had as team member at least one Spanish officer, and of course, that had everything to do with the coordination and the possibility to exchange information and to discuss things with the commander and most important officers of the Spanish Battalion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Colonel, just moving a bit more quickly through some of the background, as you've already indicated, is it correct that it was part of your regular day-to-day activities to be in communication with such organisations as UNPROFOR, the UN military observers sometimes called UNMOs, the International Committee of the Red Cross, or ICRC, UNHCR, and other, as you said, international organisations?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you briefly describe to the Chamber, because we will be looking at a number of your reports in the course of your testimony, I believe, the reporting mechanisms that you followed during your tour in the Mostar region.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Yeah. What we did as a team, we made every day a daily report, and the daily report of the teams were discussed at the CC, the coordination centre, and then by approval of all the members and approval of the chief of the CC, there was, at the end of the day, a final report of the CC that was sent to Zenica. And that was the daily routine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, as the Chamber will see for themselves in a few minutes, did it become your custom during your time there, to sign the reports or have the reports over the name of a nickname that you used called "The Flying Dutchman"?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And likewise, did Mr. Armatriain frequently use the nickname "Amigo Jesus"?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell the Chamber, please, turning to your actual time on the ground, when you first arrived in Mostar, what was the state of the -- the physical condition and the appearance of Mostar when you arrived in late May, 1993?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Well, when I went into Mostar the first time, I think it was on the 25th of May, I saw -- entering from the west side, that was, of course, the situation, I saw a quite destroyed city, and let's say going from the west bank to the east side, by passing the confrontation line, it looked like previous impressions I got from Beirut; a totally destroyed situation, actually.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell the Chamber, please, how, by what type of vehicle did you and your colleagues move around at that time?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Well, fortunately, we were travelling in an armoured Mercedes jeep.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I'll just take the opportunity to ask you this now: Was it true, sir, that during the course of your tour, that you and your colleague in a jeep were fired on and the jeep was struck by bullets on at least two occasions?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, around the time that you arrived in Mostar, did you -- was there something called a joint commission, and if you could briefly tell the Chamber what that was?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: A joint commission was actually the local three-party meeting where we tried to implement the agreements that were valid at that moment. In the beginning, it was shared by the UNMOs, the UN military observers, and later on, when they didn't enter the city any more, we took over actually. And both parties, that means from west and east side, the authorities involved were coming to the west bank and sometimes we organised it at the east bank, the east side of Mostar, to discuss all the hot items according to the ongoing agreement or the situation, the bad situation in Mostar, to relieve the situation for the people, of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To the extent that you can briefly remember, can you tell us, can you identify the representatives who typically participated in this commission on behalf of the HVO side?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Well, we had various meetings, of course, but the main players I remember very well were, from the east side, at that time Colonel Pasalic, commander 4th Armija Corps; one of his subordinates, commanders, Humo, because he was speaking also English very well; and from the HVO side, Stanko Maric, colonel of HVO in that area, and I don't remember his rank but I think he was Major Puljic, also commander of HVO at that moment. That were the people who were most of the time always a part of the meeting but it was almost depending on the issues. So what I tried to say is that the audience around the table changed according to the subjects, of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, Mr. President, if I might be allowed to assist, I'm looking at the transcript of the witness's testimony. Colonel, in line 13, Colonel Pasalic would be P-A-S-A-L-I-C, I believe commander of the 4th Armija, A-R-M-I-J-A, Corps. And I think the one officer on the line 17, it would be Puljic, which I believe, and the colonel can correct me, P-U-L-J-I-C.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, can you relate, please, to the Chamber, were there any times when people from outside of these meetings would appear at the meeting or outside the meeting and attempt to disrupt or interfere with the meetings of the joint commission?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Yeah, that happened several times that I remember once very well. We had a meeting at that time in a school building on the west side, so Colonel Pasalic was brought by UNPROFOR to the west side, and just before we started the meeting, a man with some soldiers came to the building and tried to enter the building, actually, heavily shouting but also shooting in the air.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall the name of the leader of this group?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Yeah. We asked actually our interpreter who it was, and she said, "Well, he is well known in this area as Juka."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you ever hear any full or other parts of this man's name other than Juka?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Not that I remember completely but it's in my statement due to the notes that I made at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And just briefly tell us what more, if anything, happened when Juka and these men came to the meeting? Was -- were they able, in fact, to take Colonel Pasalic out of the building?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Well, that kind of meetings were protected by UNPROFOR so there was a platoon always guarding the school. So he was not able to enter the building but the meeting was not held due to that intimidation. It was a very tense situation and, finally, UNPROFOR was able to get Pasalic and his delegation into the APC and brought them back to the east side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did you know at that time, or come to understand, to what military organisation Juka belonged?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Yeah. I am, because by the information we got in Zagreb, I got in Zagreb, actually, by the briefings of the previous members of team Mostar in Siroki Brijeg, and by all the information we got from UN, and UNPROFOR, we knew that Juka was one of the commanders, one of the Special Forces of -- used by HVO in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as part of this same briefing and information available to you, did you know who Juka's superior officer was?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Well, in that organisation, we knew that a man named Tuta was in charge of two special units; one commander was called Andabak and the other was Juka, just mentioned in this event.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned just now the name Tuta. Do you recall this morning the full name of the man called Tuta?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Well, my Serbo-Croatian is not so good but I think that his full name is Naletilic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And did you have occasion to see this Tuta during your tour in the Mostar region in 1993?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: We saw a few times, but never in Mostar itself. We saw him in his car, driving from Siroki Brijeg to Mostar or the other way around, and we saw twice or three times in Siroki Brijeg.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you saw him travelling in an automobile, can you tell the Chamber the type of automobile and whether he was accompanied by other persons?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Well, he was driving in that time I think the most expensive car in the region, a BMW from the 7 series, and always accompanied by strong, young bodyguards, armed and, let's say in my perspective, showing some macho behaviour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like the usher's assistance, please, and if you like, the binder, maybe it's easiest if the binder could be put before the witness. I think all the exhibits will be contained in the binder.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Thank.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I can direct your attention, sir, to what should be, I hope, the first document in that binder, apart from any indices that might be included, number P36.1. I would like you to look at that, please, and can you identify for the Chamber such persons shown in that photograph as you can identify.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Well, the men I know from this picture, second the left, was Stanko Maric. We dealt a lot with him because he was one of the -- he was actually the spokesman between the military HVO, HQ, headquarters in Mostar. The man with -- in the middle, to his left side, is Andabak; and Mr. Tuta was the smaller one left from Andabak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: With the glasses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Colonel, just so the record is abundantly clear, I'm going to ask you if you have a marker available there, and if not, I'll ask the usher to assist you. Could you please in a way that won't obstruct the face of these men, could you put a number 1 on the person you've identified as Stanko Maric.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you put a number 2 on the person you identified as Mr. Andabak.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And would you please put a number 3 on the person you've identified as Tuta.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just so the Chamber can see your markings, can we briefly put that on the ELMO, please. All right, thank you very much. Now, apart from seeing -- we can be finished with that for now, Usher, thank you. That should be put back in the binder. I'm reminded, of course, with the markings by the witness, that will be given a new subnumber. Thank you. Now, Colonel, you've indicated seeing Tuta several times, a number of times in the Siroki Brijeg area. Did you ever learn or see any other location where you understood this Tuta had an office or offices?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Yeah, we know because we were almost on daily basis in the MOD building downtown Mostar to see one of the officials. We know that he had an office there but we never saw him there. We never spoke actually to him because he was playing a role in the background. That was our impression.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me take your answer by way of a few points of clarification. When you say "MOD," you're talking about the HVO Ministry of Defence?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you say, "We know that he had an office there," who is the "he" you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Well, we got that information from our interpreter, who was, of course, well informed about the local situation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. But were you inside, as you said, on a daily -- often a daily basis inside this MOD building in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Yeah, many times we started on the west side to see the officials there and then we travelled through the confrontation line to the east side to speak to the officials on the east side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the course of those meetings, was one of these offices there identified to you as the office of Tuta?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I can next direct your attention, please -- and just because of numbering reasons, Mr. President, even though it's the next exhibit, obviously, in sequence, it's actually at the back of the binders -- it is Exhibit 532.1. It should be again the last document in the binders. It's titled "Bosnia and Herzegovina warring factions" and, Witness, if you could please turn to that. Can you tell the Chamber, first of all, what type of document this is and how it is - if you are - that you're familiar with it?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Are you talking about the last page?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm talking for now the document in general. You should have -- on its face it should say, "Bosnia and Herzegovina warring factions, edition number 6." It should be marked Exhibit P532.1.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Yeah. Well, this is a document provided to us by UNPROFOR.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. As reflected on the first page, is it your understanding that this document would reflect the information as stated in the lower, right corner as at 22nd July, 1993?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I can direct your attention --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would counsel please speak into the microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: My apologies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will count the pages down for everyone. I believe the 7th page, Mr. President and Witness, if you start with the first cover page itself, I believe if you go down approximately seven pages, there will be a page which -- two top boxes on that page, one on the left and one on the right, have the initials SPF. Do you have that, Witness?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: I have it, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, when you see the initials -- as a military person, you see the marking SPF, what does that mean to you?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Special Forces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And just briefly as a military -- again, as a military man familiar with these kinds of charts, is this sometimes called an ORDBAT, an order of battle?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Well, yeah, a part of the order of battle, actually.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And can you explain, looking at the box on the left side of the page, would you stop -- start at the top and work your way down through that chart and tell us in military terms what that indicates.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Well, the first box with SPF and the sign on top means a unit of regiment size but it depends, of course, of the nation and organisation how big that is. But actually, in the NATO organisation, it means at least two battalions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What you're saying now, so everyone in the courtroom is clear, when you say the marking you're referring to now, is that what we might call Roman numeral III at the top of the box?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That indicates a unit of at least something called regimental size?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Continue, please.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Then you see the first, on the left side of the box, the "1" means the number of the unit; and on the right side of the box, "SE" means southeast. Then you see the place where it was located, at least the HQ, the command post, Mostar, with a grid so YH 2898 is the grid on the map.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Then you see in -- this comes from the Spanish Battalion. You see "COM" and then a double point, "COM" stands for "commander" and then the name of the man, M. Naletilic and then his nickname Tuta. And then it's broke down in two subunits. In the structure, it means that he was in charge of the two subunits. And then you see a subunits of company size, and that means, in our terminology, 150 men, one company. Two units of the same size with their various commanders, the left unit commanded by Juka and the right commanded by Ivan Andabak. "Andavak" you see here but we know him also as Andabak. I think that the Spanish Battalion made a mistake, yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During your time in the Mostar region, starting first of all with the subbox on the far left side, that is the one marked "Juka," so far as you know, is that the same person that appeared at one or more of the joint commission meetings in Mostar in an attempt to either seize Colonel Pasalic or disrupt the meetings?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Absolutely, sir; positive.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you also tell the judges, please, in the box to the right of that, did you come to know that in fact this person Andabak or Andavak was a Special Forces commander that you encountered and met with on a number of occasions in that region during your tenure?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: That's correct. We met him several times and especially in one occasion, when he was commanding his unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, I think we will come to that in the course of your testimony later, sir. Now, Colonel, with that explanation, for which I thank you, can you tell the Chamber, please, during the approximate four months or so that you were on official assignment in the Mostar region, did you come across or learn any information that would cause you to question the accuracy of this organisational chart or, to the best of your knowledge, would you say this is an accurate portrayal of the situation on the ground?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Well, I think it was a very actual portrayal of the situation because one of the -- of the tasks of the Spanish Battalion was to update the military situation in the area, and that was done, of course, by the Intel officer and we were in close contact with the commander, the Intel officer and the operation officer of SpaBat. And this information also, we worked actually always by not one source but we tried to confirm all our information by, as much as possible, different sources. So the other sources we had actually were the UNMOS. That was a separate organisation also consisting of officers from various nations, working for the UN, and supporting actually the UNPROFOR in the area. And we had, of course, our own organisation, ECMM.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Moving forward then, away from that particular exhibit, as you took up your duties and moved around the region, did you travel frequently from Siroki Brijeg into the city of Mostar?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: On a daily basis, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you find that you typically had access to the city of Mostar, that is, you were allowed to enter the city or did that change from time to time?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Well, by our status, we had freedom of movement by the international community, actually by the EU and the international community, so most of the time we were able to do it but we had to pass at least two checkpoints on our way downtown Mostar and sometimes we were stopped and not allowed to go on, and always the reason was for our own security.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the two checkpoints that you just mentioned, which army or side, if you will, operated those checkpoints?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Well, we had to drive from Siroki Brijeg downtown Mostar always through the western part, so the checkpoints on the west side between Mostar, the entrance of Mostar and halfway, Siroki Brijeg, were manned and controlled by HVO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you -- can you relate to the Chamber by way of introduction to the next part of your testimony, did you come to hear reports that Muslim families were being evicted or expelled in the West Mostar area?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Yeah, not only reports but we heard a lot from the local people on both the west and east side, and got -- well, I have to explain that, when we were in Mostar, that was always by daytime, so we went back before darkness, also for security reasons, of course. So most of -- most of actions were done during evening and night-time so we were confronted with the results the next day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you -- before we move on further with that point, can you tell the Chamber, did that appear to you during your tour of duty in the Mostar region to be the pattern, that much of the conduct that you would hear about would take place at times when ECMM and other international observers were not in the area?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Meek?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Mr. President, Mr. Scott, my colleague, has indicated to the Trial Chamber he was going to lead this witness on background matters but I believe he's still leading the witness, and I've been quiet, but I object on leading and suggestive grounds, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Scott, rephrase your question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said a moment ago, sir, that for security reasons ECMM, the monitoring team, in your case, M2, would leave Mostar around dark and return to Siroki Brijeg; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you would hear these reports -- and I'm going to ask you about some of those in detail in a moment, but when did this conduct that you were hearing about, when was most of that conduct taking place?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: At night or during the night.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you tell the Chamber what it is you were hearing that was happening? What was being reported to you at that time?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Well, one of the sources was our interpreter because she was living on the west side and a Muslim. She reported many times the next day what she heard and what she saw. Further, it happened various times that local people stopped us, knocked on our window, and came with notes or stories about what happened last night.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: And then, of course, we had the information from the IOs and NCOs who got that kind of information also by locals. So most of the time some happenings were confirmed by different people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you tell the Chamber, by way of overview, what sort of conduct was being reported to you; what was taking place during the evening and at night when you weren't in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Well, in general, the term "ethnic cleansing" is used for that, but in Mostar especially, a lot of people was expelled from their home and sent to the east side, forced by military men most of the time. That was the overall impression we got during the whole period. And sometimes it increased more when we came -- when I came into Mostar, we heard that kind of rumours but especially in June, after the attack on the northern barracks on the east side, the situation became worse and worse, and this kind of information was increasing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In that regard, can I ask you please to go back to the first part of the binder, that's been put in front of you, and going, directing your attention to Exhibit 417.1 which should be the next exhibit after the photograph, I hope for the most part the remaining part of your testimony, the exhibits in the remaining part of your testimony, the exhibits will be more or less in order. But looking at Exhibit P417.1, can you tell us what that is and how that, if it did, came into your possession? What it means.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Yes, sir. This is a note written by our team M3 from Medjugorje. Well, the text is clear, I think. And what you see on the page is my handwriting and this was one of the notes I made at that time. Maybe it's good to explain how we come to -- how I came to such a detailed statement, because I found during the investigation, a lot of papers and even almost all my daily reports on diskette, what I put on diskette eight years ago.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Can you just, before we take turn to some of the content, you said a moment ago that the handwriting on the page, at least for the most part, is yours. For instance, on the right side, there is the notation 28 May 1993. Is that your handwriting?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: That's my handwriting and that means that I received this message and reconfirmed this message at that day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it seems to be, I won't say signed, but over -- the text seems to be above and over a reference called "Tertio." Can you tell us what that means?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: "Tertio" means 3, as you know, and it stands for M3, the team from Medjugorje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, directing your attention to the note itself, on the second line, it says, "The male persons [Mike of course]..." Now can you explain to the Chamber what the reference to "Mike" means?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Yes, "Mike" means the explanation for the letter M in the NATO spelled alphabet, and it means here Muslim. Male persons. Muslim male persons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you say, I think most of the text probably speaks for itself and if the judges have questions, they will have an opportunity, Colonel, to ask you about that later. I won't spend too much time on it in the interests of time. Below that, again, in is it your writing where it says "100 confirmed cases"?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: That means that, with this message, we got a lot of information downtown at that day what confirmed this message actually by locals. So I made a small note and said, well, at least it should be 100 persons who were expelled actually.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell the Chamber, in terms of your working practices or the ECMM's practices, perhaps, what does it mean to say "confirmed"?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: "Confirmed" means that initial information we got, let's say what starts as a rumour, is confirmed by other sources and then it makes the information quite reliable, and we only call it confirmed information when it at least was coming from two or more different sources.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say under "100 confirmed cases," it says, if I read it correctly - and correct me if I'm wrong -"occupation of houses/apartments by HVO." What does that refer to?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Well, that refers to the pattern of working. What happened was that people were expelled, Muslim people, and their houses were occupied by HVO soldiers. They put immediately, for instance, stickers on the door and changed the name on the door. We saw that. We went to places where we saw the change of names actually.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was my next question. Directing your attention to approximately the 1st of June, 1993, did you have the opportunity to see some of this in your own eyes -- with your own eyes?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell the Chamber what you observed at that time.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Once we had the opportunity after picking up our interpreter, the opportunity to go to a place where such a thing happened by her information, because that night she was informed about what happened to a family, we went to that place and saw what was the result of that night, and I took some photographs of that place as a kind of proof, of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you just describe to the Chamber what you saw, what was the condition of the apartment when you saw it at that time.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Well, we saw that the door was damaged, I don't -- can't remember exactly what it was but it looks like that it was hit by a bullet at least, and inside the house and the room we entered, we saw bullet impacts in the ceiling and it was an enormous mess. It seems to be a place what was searched and maybe looted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, can you -- do you recall on about that same day, the 1st of June, 1993, was one of the occasions when the joint commission had a meeting in West Mostar?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Well, I think so. When it's in the statement, for sure that is correct. I don't know by heart all the meetings we had, of course, with daytime group.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of course, and we are going to go to some of your reports in fairly short order. Let me ask you this way and then if we need to refer to your report, I'll ask the Chamber's permission to show you your report so you can refresh your memory. But the times when you mentioned Juka Prazina coming to these meetings, did that happen only once or more than once?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Once that we were really threatened but we saw him a second time strolling around the place actually with his men. But it was once that he really tried to enter the building and was threatening Colonel Pasalic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I want to turn your attention for a few moments to the hospital that was on the east side of Mostar. During the course of your duties there, did you visit the East Mostar hospital on a number of occasions?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: That's correct, sir. We had on daily base, when it was possible, a visit to the headquarters of the Armija. And most of the time we visited there also other authorities and one of the important places at that time was the war hospital.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you briefly describe to the Chamber, and I will tell you Colonel, the Chamber has heard or received some information about the hospital already, but what was the general conditions at the hospital on the occasions when you were there?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Well, especially in the month of June, the situation in the war hospital was very, very bad. And what we did, we had was the chef de clinique most of the time contact to deal with, to hear from him the problems he had. At that time I very well remember that they were operating 24 hours, around the clock, with a very small group of specialists under, let's say, circumstances that was very, very, very bad.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. What was the nature, if you can tell us briefly, about the supply or availability of medical equipment and medicine?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Well, at that time, the east bank was isolated and there was no support for the war hospital from the west side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did there come a time when Colonel Pasalic asked if some medical supplies or personnel could be provided from the hospital in the Croat or west part of Mostar?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Yeah, we got a request, official request signed by Pasalic to support the war hospital on the east side by a proposal to exchange specialists from the west to the east bank and vice versa, and also later on, when we contacted the chef de clinique of the war hospital, there came the requests for the most important medication and medical equipment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now was one of the persons you dealt with at the HVO hospital a person named Ivan Bagaric?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was his position or title there, what was his role there?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: When I recall well, he was in charge of the hospital or the deputy at that moment, but that changed sometimes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you meet with this Mr. Bagaric on a number of occasions?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Yeah, because he was in charge and actually the spokesman to us and we tried to establish that exchange and tried to get medication and medical equipment from the west side to the east side and he was actually the spokesman so we dealt with him all the time, or most of the time I have to say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you briefly describe to the Chamber how in your experience Mr. Bagaric was dressed and equipped at the time that you met -- at the times you met with him.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Well, it was not exactly the picture I have from a chef de clinique or a specialist, a doctor. Well, he was wearing a white doctor's coat, but under that coat he was wearing his camouflage uniform and he was armed with a pistol.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did there come a time, however, when some medical supplies were provided by the HVO hospital in West Mostar that were then transmitted or communicated to the east side hospital?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: That's correct. Well, actually, we took a lot of effort to get some of the list from the west side to the east side, but not the most -- the badly-needed equipment, for instance, oxygen and ambulance which they were asking for, was not provided. So we are talking then about bandages and medication.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Directing your attention to around the 11th of June 1993, was this an occasion when some medical supplies were in fact transported from the west side to the east side hospital?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: That's correct. We were able, at the end, to organise and transport by UNPROFOR from the west to the east bank to bring the first part of the medical stuff to the east side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was an UNPROFOR officer killed on that day while this shipment of medical supplies was being made?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Unfortunately, the platoon commander, who was standing above his APC, was instantly killed by sniper fire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that a Spanish Battalion officer by the name of Lieutenant Aguilar?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your military experience, did you come to have any understanding of how it was that he was killed; the type of ammunition that was used and the approximate location from which the shot came?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Yeah, it happened in the evening. We were not there but, of course, by the information of various authorities, the Spanish Battalion, for instance, UNSFPO, the UN civilian police --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Meek?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, I object. There is an absolute lack of foundation. This witness has already testified he was not present, his group and unit was not present. It's pure speculation, we're going into the area of pure speculation at this point and I object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Meek, let us hear the whole story and then we will make the right conclusion after the testimony of this witness. You may continue, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. By all the information we got, and by our experience, driving from the west to the east side and the place where the officer was hit -- the place, I mean the situation -- the place exactly where the APC was hit, made very clear to us that the bullet was fired from the west bank, and by our experience of the situation, even by shot almost at the same place earlier, it should come from the blue bank building on the west side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it may assist the Chamber for the record purposes, when you say "blue bank building," what does that mean? What building did that describe or represent to you?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Well, on the HVO west side, I have to say on the west side, HVO was manning an old bank building with blue glasses. I think that it was 11 storeys, 11 -- I miss the name of -- 11 floors, sorry, 11 floors, was manned by snipers, they -- and it was a building that dominated actually the confrontation line. And they had a line of sight from that building through the so-called Tito bridge in the middle of the centre, up to the eastern side. So it was possible from that building to oversee that part of the road and the bridge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, skipping a couple of exhibits which we will come back to -- as I indicated earlier, the documents are not exactly, for various reasons, in the order of your testimony, but if I could direct your attention and the courtroom's attention, please, to Exhibit P451.1, which they should be, Mr. President, should be able to find the documents in numerical exhibit number order, so if you proceed through the binder, you should be able to come to Exhibit 451.1. And Witness, I'll ask you just a couple of questions about this document before, I think, the 11.00 recess. Is Exhibit 451.1 a letter or a communication that was received by ECMM at that time or dated the 12th of June 1993, by this commander ABIH commander named Pasalic?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: I'm sorry, sir, but I didn't find so far the document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you keep, hopefully, going down through your binder, it may be some pages because there is both an English version and a translation of these documents, so it may take you some pages but if you will just keep leafing through the binder, please, until you get to Exhibit 451.1. Perhaps the usher can assist. It's dated the 12th of June, 1993.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Right, yeah. Got it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just to repeat my question, and then we are kind of approaching now at this point the 11.00 hour, but can you just tell us, is that a communication that ECMM received around this time from the ABIH commander Pasalic?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did it happen on a number of occasions that Colonel Pasalic would bring a protest or objections or things to the ECMM's attention?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, directing your attention to the next to last paragraph of that letter, can you confirm to the Chamber that it was approximately on the 11th of June, 1993, when this UNPROFOR contingent was fired on in which Lieutenant Aguilar was killed?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: That's correct, sir. But I have to say, of course, that both parties in our investigation and our questions, accused each other, of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. As you said a moment ago -- and this will be my last question, Mr. President, before the recess, if that's the Chamber's desire. Were you able to determine nonetheless, sir, from which side of -- given the way that Mr. -- excuse me, Lieutenant Aguilar was struck, from which side of the confrontation line the shot came that killed Lieutenant Aguilar?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, yes, Mr. Meek?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, my objection is that question has been asked and answered. It's repetitive.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Scott, we also believe that the witness has answered this question already.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. President, I would suggest that that's a time, a convenient point to stop.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Usher, would you please take the witness out of the room first. We will resume at 11.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Scott, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, I apologise for any discourtesy that might have appeared; I failed to introduce the Chamber to Ms. Marie-Ursula Kind who will be standing in for Ms. Fleming for a couple of days. My apologies for not introducing her sooner.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Colonel, I'm going to try to shorten my questions related to the hospital on the east side of Mostar down to two or three, if I can. Did you engage in a number of discussions through your tour of duty in the Mostar region with Mr. Bagaric and others in an attempt to obtain assistance from the HVO for the medical conditions on the east -- in East Mostar?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you just simply relate to the Chamber at the end of the day, so to speak, by the end of your tour, how much if any assistance had the HVO side in fact provided?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Well, the bottom line actually was of our -- all our efforts, that there came no exchange of specialists, and once medical equipment, well, let's say medical supplies, were brought to the east, another time I think that we brought some to Jablanica, but that was -- that was all. That means that there were a lot of preconditions and the willingness, at the end, of HVO to secure the whole operation was never -- never established.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, moving on, apart from the hospital to the conditions in East Mostar in general, can you briefly describe to the Chamber what you observed in terms of the supply of food and water in East Mostar at that time.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: We are talking, for instance, about the month of June, it became worse and worse. The running water has to come from the west side by two pipelines and over the river Neretva, so it was controlled at the west side, and I remember that in a certain time bracket, one of the supplies was stopped. It means that all the population on the east side were in trouble, and especially, of course, the war hospital, by having no running water. Also the food situation became more and more bad due to the impossibility to get UNHCR convoys to the east bank, so they ran out of water, they ran out of food.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you approach representatives on the HVO side about allowing humanitarian aid into East Mostar, and if so, what was the response?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: We did that all the time to get the UNHCR and the Red Cross also into town and to the east, at the east side, but due to the dangerous situation, the increasing of shellings and sniper fire, they decided not to enter the city any more or visit the east bank. So for security reasons, they didn't show up, and at the very last, we were the only international organisation, by our armoured jeep, who were able to cross and to visit all the places on the west and east side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I can ask you to look next at -- and I hope this one will be easier to find, back toward the beginning of the binder, if I can ask your attention, please, to be given to Exhibit P435.1.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: 11th of June, you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I believe the letter itself is dated the 7th of June so perhaps a bit further in the other direction for the beginning.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you just tell the Chamber what that document is.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Well, this is one of the protest letters we received in copy from the commander of the 4th Armija Corps, Colonel Pasalic, that describes the situation on the east bank.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And for instance, on the top of the -- upper right corner of the first -- very corner, but the upper right part, portion of the first page, does appear to be addressed to ECMM?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: That's correct. That are we. That means he handed it over to us, and on the second page, you see that it was additional sent to UNPROFOR, the Red Cross, UNHCR and HVO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, Colonel, if you can just look at the text of that document for a moment or two, just ask you one or two questions about it. But I'll give you a chance to look at it for a moment.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Well, in general, this -- these are complaints he made to us many times by our visits and now he put that once more on paper.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to ask you, Colonel, without -- I'm not asking you to agree to the particular terminology or some of the adjectives, perhaps, that Mr. Pasalic, Colonel Pasalic used, but in terms of the conditions that are described, in terms of, for instance, the hospital, the food and water situation in East Mostar, would you agree that that was an accurate statement of the conditions that then existed?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: I agree on -- upon the overall situation he describes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you just tell the Chamber what was your practice when these sorts of communications would come from persons such as Pasalic and perhaps others? Would you communicate these things on to, for instance, again as we heard this morning, RC Zenica?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: That's correct. We checked if the parties mentioned on the second page sent to were informed and we always added this as copy to our reports to Zenica. From all this official letters from both sides, we always attached that to our reports to Zenica and to our own organisation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you just briefly confirm to the Chamber on about the 7th of June, 1993, was your vehicle fired on again? Just briefly relate that, those facts to the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Correct. That happened when it was the second time on our way from Medjugorje back to Mostar. Well, first we thinking about flat tire but we found out by inspecting the car that it was another direct hit actually by a bullet.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, apart from rifle fire, can you tell the Chamber, were you ever -- was your vehicle ever fired upon by some sort of explosive shell or device?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Well, we had another bad experience, I don't remember exactly when it was but you can find that in my statement, very close to the confrontation line and close to the blue bank building, we -- when we were out of the vehicle, into a building, a rocket was fired just -- just near the vehicle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "just near the vehicle," can you tell the Chamber approximately what distance, if you recall, the impact of the shell or rocket to your vehicle?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Between five and ten metres. But the effect of an anti-armour grenade is enormous on that distance, of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you just describe to the Chamber a little bit more about this vehicle that you were driving? Frankly, Colonel, I have not put certain other materials in the record just because of the abundance of the material that the Chamber already is confronted with but can you just describe the vehicle that you were driving throughout your tour of duty. What did it look like and how would it appear to people seeing it?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Well, it was, as I said before, a Mercedes armoured jeep, provided by the German government, and it was painted white with big orange letters, ECMM. On the antenna, we had our blue flag, so for everyone in the area it was very, very clear that that was the ECMM mission driving around. And also we were at that time all the time actually dressed in white uniforms -- well, not uniforms but white suits, actually.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By the way, can you tell the Chamber, were you during your time in Bosnia as an ECMM member, were you or other ECMM members ever armed?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: No, not being a military organisation, we were not armed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was that -- to your knowledge, was that fact widely known?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: For sure because we were on daily basis dealing with all the parties so they know exactly who we were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, before we move on, this rocket or shell that you've mentioned, you mentioned this was in close proximity to what you've described as the blue bank building. Were you ever -- were you able to make any determination or observation as to approximately where that shell had come from?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Well, the only possibility, according to the place and the distance and the impact of the projectile, it should be fired from the blue bank building. I don't know why, but it's easily, it's an easy guess to intimidate us. I hope so, that that was the reason, and not to hit us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've mentioned this morning already a man named Stanko Maric. Was he one of the persons you met with on the HVO side on a number of occasions?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Many times because he was the military spokesman to us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was his role or position, as best as you came to understand it at that time?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Well, he gave the official answers upon our questions and that were, of course, questions directed directly to the military HVO organisation, and he was, of course, always a part in the beginning of the -- of the joint commission meetings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell the Chamber, please, Colonel, based on the words that Mr. Maric said and the conduct that you observed, what appeared to be his political position or views about what was happening in Mostar at that time?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Well, most of the time, the official standpoint of HVO was that they controlled the situation on the west bank and when something occurred where they didn't had an explanation for, then sometimes but not often, they referred to uncontrolled elements, criminal elements, I have to say, and that they were working on law and order, to get rid of these or to catch these criminal elements. He particularly showed to be a strong nationalist, for -- in all HVO matters, actually. So he was quite a tough guy to discuss with hot items and we always had, of course, let's say, hot questions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell the Chamber, please, and again drawing on your professional military experience and specifically your experience while in the Mostar region in 1993, can you share any observation with the Chamber about the explanation that these various bad acts were only being carried out by so-called uncontrolled, criminal elements?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Well, by all the knowledge, everything we saw and heard at that time, we don't believe that that was the right answer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell the Chamber why you say that?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: We think, and we had a lot of indications, actually, that, for instance, ethnic cleansing, expelling people from the west to the east bank, was well organised, and not only by a few criminal elements. That's, when you talk about the numbers, for instance, almost impossible, and it was always done, of course, by night, that has to be done very quickly and well organised. Otherwise, it's impossible to do so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before coming back to some of those in fact events, expulsions, let me turn your attention to a place called the Heliodrom. Did you have an opportunity to visit the Heliodrom during your assignment in the Mostar region?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: We had, sir. It was one of our jobs to get access to, on both sides, the prisons. So by the permission of the deputy chief of the military police, Mr. Pusic, we went to the Heliodrom to do an inquiry actually at that place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
