utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, I think the interpretation is quite good but the name is very difficult to be recorded correctly. You should not blame the interpretations.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no. That was not my intention but the meaning was changed. Maybe there was a misunderstanding. When the witness says a place we called Visnje, Visnje is cherry. Then the witness explained but this did not -- was not included in the transcript. I was just trying to be of assistance, I'm not trying to criticise the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Prosecutor, would you please make it clear for us.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Yes, I will try.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just to resolve this problem, I would ask Mr. Ajanic just to repeat the names of places you performed job, but slowly, please.

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC
utterances.text: Buna, the airport, Hortije, we call it Visnje, which is a fruit orchard, and that's where we dug trenches. Near the Ero Hotel, Vrdi, and at Stela's.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you are talking about Stela's location, which part of Mostar do you mean?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC
utterances.text: I'm referring to the Croatian part.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps you remember the name --

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC
utterances.text: The Kalemova Street.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What kind of job did you perform?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC
utterances.text: I would clean the rooms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what about the rest of the prisoners? What kind of job did they perform?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC
utterances.text: They came for us, two Strumfs and a taxi driver. He was a taxi driver before the war, I can't remember his name now. They picked up 25 of us, as far as I can recollect. However...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ajanic, just I would ask you to stop at this point. Perhaps you have not understood me. And first my remark to the transcript. Just paragraph 17, the name of the street Kalemova is missing. Mr. Ajanic told us that it was Kalemova Street where he worked for Stela.

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Kallemova, K-A-L-L-E-M-O-V-A.

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC
utterances.text: K-A-L-E-M-O-V-A. Maybe I'm having some problems because I have some teeth missing. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ajanic, just to return to our previous question, what kind of job did prisoners perform, for example, in Buna airport and other places just mentioned by yourself?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC
utterances.text: I worked with other prisoners there, not with these.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm just asking you about other prisoners. I do not ask you about some definite prisoners.

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC
utterances.text: We were digging and carrying sandbags. We were digging trenches and carrying sacks mostly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you carry out your job when there was shooting in the area?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC
utterances.text: Yes. They chased us into the crossfire, then our men realised that we were prisoners and then they didn't shoot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you have mentioned the name of some person whom you called Stela. Do you know his real name?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC
utterances.text: Vinko.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember his full name?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC
utterances.text: Martinovic. Yes, I knew him much better before the war. He was a taxi driver, and I can point him out to you, if you wish.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, if you can do it, please, you may do it.

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC
utterances.text: Wearing a dark suit with a tie, next to Tuta.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On which desk, at which desk is he sitting now?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC
utterances.text: At the last -- in the last row, the first next to the policeman on the left, so he is right next to him; and Tuta has grey hair and is sitting next to him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ajanic. But did Vinko Martinovic know you?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC
utterances.text: Yes, quite well. We were even neighbours for a time, and you can ask him also. He will tell you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know other members of his family?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC
utterances.text: I did; I knew his father and Zvonko, his father's brother, who is a taxi driver to this day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what position he occupied during the war? I mean Mr. -- Stela.

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC
utterances.text: As far as I was able to understand, they referred to him as, "General."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know to which unit he belonged?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC
utterances.text: Just a moment. Vinko Skrobo, the Convicts Battalion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who was his commander?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC
utterances.text: Do you mean who was superior to him, who had a higher rank?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, exactly.

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC
utterances.text: As far as I was able to understand, I think Tuta was superior.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What makes you think so?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC
utterances.text: Because that's what I think. A couple of times I would hear him asking the other, instead of the other way around, and Tuta has a nickname, which is "Stari," which means old man.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know any other soldiers from Stela's unit?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC
utterances.text: Yes. I did, but I can't remember the names.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you just mentioned that you worked for Stela's unit. Did you work for him on one occasion only?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC
utterances.text: On one occasion as a prisoner, and later, I worked perhaps several times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I would ask you about your work for Stela as a prisoner. Could you tell the Trial Chamber, when did it happen?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC
utterances.text: I can't remember the date but if you want me to give you the details, please let me do so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. But first I will ask you some questions and then I will ask you to just recount the whole story. Do you remember who picked you up from Heliodrom and took to Stela's place?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC
utterances.text: The two Strumf brothers and this taxi driver. He was a taxi driver before the war. I can't remember now exactly. He was a driver of a Deutz, and it belonged to a Vajda Krilic, 110 C10. It was a blue pickup truck and I used to work with him before the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please repeat the full name of brothers. Because it is not entered in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC
utterances.text: Whose name?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The brothers that took you from Heliodrom.

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC
utterances.text: I think the taxi driver's name was Vlaho. He drove the Deutz.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you just mentioned two brothers who also --

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC
utterances.text: The Strumf brothers. They are the sons of the late Ivan Culo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. How many prisoners did they take from Heliodrom on that day?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please and now recount how it happened on that day.

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC
utterances.text: We came in the Deutz in front of Stela's barracks and they lined us up two by two. However, they separated me and Mujo Tuto. I think his real name is Mustafa and his nickname is Tuto, and he's a car mechanic, an electrician. We waited in front of the barracks for Stela to come and when he arrived, he said, "Do you know where you are?" We said we do. "Will you do what I tell you? If you won't, tell me." However, we said yes. And then he left me and Mujo Tuto to clean the rooms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ajanic, I would ask you to slow down because I think that the interpreters may have some problems.

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC
utterances.text: However, the 23 people were taken away and I went to -- also to the locality in the Liska Street where the hospital was before the war. It was the emergency section of the hospital. At one point, I happened to be cleaning Stela's office. He also happened to be there. Somebody knocked on the door and said, "General, sir, here he is. He's starting to run away." And Stela asked him, "Who is it?" And the other guy said, "Neno Armandic," but I swear by everything and I guarantee that Neno just said, "I did not try it, Stela. You can be sure of that." And Stela said, "Take him downstairs, don't beat him."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ajanic, stop for one moment because again there are some problems with the transcript. Please repeat the name of the prisoner who was accused of just trying to escape.

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC
utterances.text: Ernest Takac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ajanic, you have not understood me rightly. Who was Ernest Takac?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC
utterances.text: I think he was a soldier of Tuta -- of Stela's, in uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And now I ask you to repeat the name of prisoner he brought to Stela's office.

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC
utterances.text: Neno Armandic. Before the war, he was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [no interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Unit, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I didn't get interpretation. Would you please try again.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Oh, yes, I'm reading the transcript and I'm also listening to what the witness is saying, and I think the interpretation of these attempts by my learned friend the Prosecutor to find out who brought him and who was there, it now turns out that it's a soldier of Tuta's, and then two dashes, and then Stela's, in uniform, so could we please clarify that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ajanic, we were talking about Ernest Takac. You told just that you thought that he was soldier of some unit. Which unit?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC
utterances.text: Since he came to Stela, I think he was a soldier of Stela's, but I don't know because he addressed him as, "Mr. General, sir."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. I think that now the question is clarified.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: And I would like the Trial Chamber to know that our witness has some problems with his hearing so sometimes it's quite possible that he may misunderstand me. That's why I'm trying to speak very slowly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: I think the witness is also a little bit nervous, so we should really treat him gently. He did correct himself on the transcript. He said a soldier of Tuta and corrected himself straight away to Stela, so I think he's very nervous and give him sometime and we'll get there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So Mr. Ajanic, you may go ahead with your story that happened on that day.

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC
utterances.text: However, Enes Takac took Neno Armandic downstairs to the basement and you could hear a loud scream, but Mujo Tuta and I were trying to carry out a garbage can and we saw five or six soldiers on the stairs and we went into a room. Somebody called me, however, they called me Lopata, and told me to come here. I came downstairs and among the people there was Stela, and he told me, "Hit him or you will get the same thing that he is going to get." I started to hit him but I couldn't do it. I said, "Whoever was whatever they were will be that again." And they just laughed and they told me to go into the room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ajanic, just stop for one moment. You were talking about some person being beaten. Whom do you mean? Who was beaten?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC
utterances.text: Neno Armandic, and I've known him for 20 years.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps you can spell his full name, if you can, please.

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC
utterances.text: N-E-N-O A-R-M-A-N-E-D-Z [as interpreted]. I'm not really good with words so I apologise, because of my teeth.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you just told us that you knew him before the war.

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC
utterances.text: Yes. I was also the one among those that he took to the MUP.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. You may go ahead with the story.

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC
utterances.text: Well, maybe they had a drink or something. Anyway, when I came back into the room, he started to scream again. This stopped for a while and somebody backed a car all the way next to the wall of Stela's barracks. Then they took out Neno, two or three soldiers took him out, soldiers whom I don't know. The first left. I mean the right mud guard. They -- excuse me for saying this but they peed into cans of beer, empty beer cans and gave that to him to drink. But one of them took out - please, excuse me - the worst thing and he placed it in his mouth and he asked him, "Do you like this?" And he replied, "Yes, I do." Then we were -- for a while, I was in a room and he took out -- Stela took Mujo Tuta home to take a bath and perhaps to eat something and then he brought him back with two bags in his hand and I asked Mujo, "Where were you?" And he said, "I went and I took a bath," and he also fixed something on Stela's car. There was something wrong with the electrical installation of Stela's car. And he brought back two bags. However, for a while, the people came who were out on the construction site, we were lined up by one soldier, whom I don't remember, and then later Stela came and he said, "Do you know where you are?" Some people said yes, some people were silent and so on. "What you saw you did not see. What you heard, you have not heard. And please understand what can happen to you, too." And he told the driver, Vlaho, take these 24 people to the Heliodrom, and this one person tell -- say that he tried to escape and he was left behind. And that was Neno Armandic, and he stayed behind us and he was in the place where you repair cars and he was covered by boards.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he ever return to Heliodrom -- I mean Neno Armandic?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC
utterances.text: No. And later I heard that he was transferred to Hit, where the Sarajevo bank is, and he was dead. He disappeared. I personally don't know to this day where his grave is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ajanic, let's return to the morning of that day, to the moment when the people from Stela's unit were picking up prisoners for job. Did you see Neno Armandic in the morning, before you were taken to Stela's place?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC
utterances.text: Let me tell you, when Stela's unit came, these two brothers, the Strumf brothers, the sons of Ivan Culo, specially asked for Neno Armandic, who was in room number 1, and he escaped to room number 5. And Hamica Siptar gave him away. That's what they called him. He gave Neno Armandic away. He said, "I know where he is." And the two of them and Hamica went and brought him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In what condition was he when you saw him in the morning?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC
utterances.text: He looked well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In what condition was he when you saw him last on that day?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC
utterances.text: God forbid anybody to have to go through that, and I wouldn't like to respond to that question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But still I think that the Trial Chamber would like to know a little bit about his condition. I understand that it's a very sad story and it's very difficult for you, but still, this is a courtroom and this is the last chance for you for speaking out. Please try to recall.

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC
utterances.text: I will also tell you this honestly and clearly: I feel much -- the first time, he was bloody; the second time, he was black and blue; and the third time, he looked as if he had gained at least 15 or 20 kilogrammes, so imagine -- you can imagine what he looked like.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And now again, I understand that you feel a little bit shy but you just told the Trial Chamber about "the worst thing" that was put into Armandic's mouth. I think that you should, I'm sorry, call a spade a spade.

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC
utterances.text: Well, let me say this; it's somewhat rude, if you will excuse me. I don't know how to say it. We say that we call it penis.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ajanic, did you tell about this incident to the investigator when you were being interviewed?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC
utterances.text: No, because they -- I was always questioned by women and, to tell you the truth, I was ashamed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And just to clarify one more question, talking about Armandic, was he a policeman or the civilian police?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC
utterances.text: He was an agent for thieves, for robberies, for robbers, for drug addicts. There it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ajanic, could you describe Stela's headquarter building, headquarters building. If you remember, of course.

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC
utterances.text: I remember it well and even -- if I saw it, I could show you the exact office, even if it was in a hundred different ways, I could still get the address, the exact address.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: First of all, I would like you to describe the building itself, from the outside.

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC
utterances.text: Yes. Because the Chetnik war had gone on before, the building was somewhat neglected. It looked -- it was situated in a nice park. There was a garage in front of it, the entrance was from the Kalemova Street, the vehicle entrance, and then I can't remember exactly, but from the Rondo was the pedestrian entrance, for example, the owners of the apartments. And downstairs, when you entered, there was a cellar, the first floor. On the second floor was Stela's office, it was a door to the left. When you entered the room, Stela's desk was on the left and his chair. To this day I remember a white telephone.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, I would ask you to show the witness Exhibit number 15.7P.

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC
utterances.text: This is it. This is the telephone. This is the heater.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just take the pointer and --

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC
utterances.text: This is the telephone, this is his chair. This is where the door is, or the window, I can't remember precisely where the door is. That's where you would go in, and they would usually be sitting, his soldiers, they would be sitting here. Also I would sit there when I had coffee with him. There was a chair here, I think. This is his office. This is his telephone. These are his papers. These are the windows, and I think that this is where the door is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ajanic, do you mean that you entered that office on that day when all this story happened to Armandic?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC
utterances.text: Yes. I did go in that day and afterwards, when my child was killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So Mr. Ajanic, you were returned to Heliodrom on the same day?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know how the HVO soldiers explained the fact that Armandic was missing in Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, we don't know that. We don't know that. We, the detainees, didn't know that. We were handed over to the military police and what they talked about amongst themselves, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long were you kept in Heliodrom after that accident with Armandic?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC
utterances.text: For about two months. Then I went to a work location close to the Hotel Ero when I saw a HVO soldier whom I knew very well. When I was taken from my apartment to the Heliodrom, my wife stayed behind. She was pregnant. She gave birth. I didn't know this. I asked him, "Did my wife give birth?" And he said, "Yes, she did. I will tell you about it." But he didn't tell me about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened then?

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC
utterances.text: Then I went to the Hotel Ero, where I knew a person called Drago Kordo, he was in the transport business and he was in a unit, I don't remember the name of the unit, and I asked him, his name is Drago Kordo. We called him --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't catch the nickname.

utterances.speaker: HALIL AJANIC
utterances.text: So he was surprised when he saw me. I asked him, "Cigo, could you please go to my house and see if my wife has given birth?" However, he went home and he brought back the news that my wife was well and she was fine but that the baby was dead. And I'm asking you if you would permit me to smoke a cigarette, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Maybe we should have a break, then, because the witness is really nervous and this is a very -- he's supposed to tell two very sad stories to the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we will have an early break. Witness, I have to remind you that you are still under the oath so do not talk to anybody about your testimony today and do not let anybody talk to you about it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I will not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: So you may leave now. We will resume at 9.30 tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 8th day of January, 2002, at 9.30 a.m. 22 23 24 25
